engine_gap.behavior: Extracting behavior units from a large decompose-set (136 files, per 10-inventory) within a bounded number of actor turns, so a harvest run covers every decomposed file rather than leaving most of them unreached because one turn ran out of room.
source_evidence: 20-harvest/output/coverage-note.md: coverage note, 118 of 136 decompose files/partition-members not reached this run

why_each_fails.stage: A stage boundary is fixed at workflow-definition time in workflow.toml's stages list; it cannot be multiplied dynamically per-run based on how many files a given subject repository's inventory happens to contain, so it cannot express 'as many turns as this file count needs' without the workflow author guessing the count in advance.
why_each_fails.helper: A helper is deterministic machinery (enumerate, hash, normalize) and can enumerate or hash file bytes, but cannot perform the judgment call of recognizing an independently-triggerable behavior in prose and drafting its statement/trigger/outcome/authority fields — that judgment is exactly the actor work this stage exists to do, so delegating extraction itself to a helper would not be extraction, it would be skipping it.

engine_gap.minimum_runtime_capability_required: The runtime would need to own a durable fan-out: the ability for one stage to spawn a bounded set of actor sub-turns over a partitioned input set (here, 10-inventory's own file partitions), each producing its own share of behavior-units.ndjson, with the runtime — not the actor — tracking which partitions are done/pending/failed and aggregating the results deterministically before the stage is considered complete.
engine_gap.observable_acceptance_test: Given a decompose set larger than one turn can read in full, running 20-harvest to completion produces one behavior-units.ndjson covering every decomposed file with no 'not reached' partition remaining, and the run's own journal shows more than one actor turn was used to produce it, with the daemon (not the actor) tracking partition completion and retrying any partition a sub-turn failed to finish.

engine_gap.behavior: Giving a per-run disposition (promote/evidence) to durable content this run writes outside any stage's own output/ directory — specifically, the materialized draft workflow packages under .sergeant/drafts/workflows/ — so scripts/finalize.py's mechanical apply can decide whether that content survives the run's closing commit the same way it already decides for a stage's own output/ content.
source_evidence: 60-draft/output/draft-report.md: 'Meta-level grammar pressure, for 90-reconcile' section — 'the D9 disposition/finalize mechanism ... only governs a stage's own output/ — it has no lower-rung way to give per-run content written elsewhere in the worktree a disposition, or to bring it under ../scripts/finalize.py's reach'

why_each_fails.stage: A stage's own output/README.md disposition table (docs/icm/convention.md §1a) only binds filenames literally present under that same stage's own output/ directory — scripts/finalize.py's parse_readme only ever looks inside <stage>/output/, so no stage's own CONTEXT.md or README.md, however it is worded, can extend a disposition claim to a sibling tree like .sergeant/drafts/workflows/.
why_each_fails.helper: scripts/finalize.py is exactly this kind of helper, and by its own documented design explicitly excludes .sergeant/drafts/workflows/<candidate>/'s own output/ directories from its reach (they are that candidate's future-run declarations, not this run's artifacts). Extending a helper to also own disposition semantics for an entire separate tree written by a different stage is no longer deterministic invoked-by-a-stage machinery — deciding what survives a run is durable authority the runtime would have to own, not a helper's.

engine_gap.minimum_runtime_capability_required: The runtime would need to own a per-run disposition registry that is not scoped to exactly one stage's own output/ directory — a durable fact naming, for content written anywhere under the worktree during a run (not only <stage>/output/), whether it promotes into the Work-branch merge or is evidence-only — so a workflow whose principal deliverable is materialized outside any single stage's output/ (like draft workflow packages) can still receive a real, finalize-honored disposition instead of being invisible to scripts/finalize.py.
engine_gap.observable_acceptance_test: After a repo-to-icm run materializes packages under .sergeant/drafts/workflows/, running the finalize helper reports and applies a disposition decision (keep or remove) for each materialized package path exactly as it already does for <stage>/output/<file>, without any stage inventing an ad hoc README convention outside the documented D9 mechanism to obtain that coverage.
